originality.rationale: Direct comparison of full statements: no inspected prior theorem gives the all-distance paired-tree wheel transfer polynomial and the positive-variance Gaussian constants. Known complementary-tree endpoints, wheel two-edge covariances, and signed-Walsh singularity classifications are strictly weaker than the reported complete overlap distribution. Bóna–Wagner 2025 treats dense and other graph families, not wheel geometry. Unindexed equivalent symbolic evaluations remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed bivariate Tutte/random-cluster or two-forest transfer identity may encode an equivalent polynomial without explicitly naming wheel Euclidean chords.
The 2025 independent-tree intersection article supplies a broad method, although its inspected theorems do not include wheels.
The geometric invariant is mathematically dual to a standard basis-exchange distance enumerator, so different terminology could hide a prior exact formula.

value.rationale: The complete all-order Euclidean chord multiplicity polynomial is a natural metric invariant of labelled graphic matroid base polytopes, contains m+1 distinct distance shells, and yields explicit Gaussian behavior distinct from dense-graph Poisson overlap. It strictly refines prior complementary-tree extremal enumeration and low-order covariance, with motivated applications to geometry of uniformly sampled vertices.
